question.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨0,8,-1⟩+t⟨-1,1,7⟩+s⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-1,1,7⟩$ and $w=⟨3,-5,1⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & 7 \\ 3 & -5 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =36i+22j+2k \\  & =⟨36,22,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨36,22,2⟩.$
